title: Transmigration handoff protocol and upgrade gateway for private clusters
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Goal: build a lightweight, transactional handoff protocol and an upgrade gateway that orchestrates multi-stage schema and runtime migrations for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) clusters with minimal application downtime and clear rollback semantics. This ticket covers the protocol spec, a coordinator service prototype, preflight hooks for health/compatibility checks, and a rollout gate integration with the Console's rollout engine.

Scope and constraints:
- Must support LTS channel pinning and allow customers to opt into staged feature releases.
- Handle heterogeneous clusters (mixed node types and mixed minor runtime versions) without requiring full cluster drain.
- Provide idempotent, resumable migrations for database schema changes and agent binary upgrades.
- Operate in air-gapped environments: artifact delivery via customer-provided registries or S3 proxies.
- Minimal privileged changes: leverage existing control-plane RPCs where possible; avoid new wide-scope permissions.

Design overview:
1) Transmigration handoff protocol (THP): a small state machine for each cluster upgrade run with explicit states: PREPARE -> SNAPSHOT -> MIGRATE -> VALIDATE -> COMMIT -> FINALIZE. Each state exposes deterministic checks and compensating actions for rollback. THP messages are signed and stored in the cluster's upgrade ledger for observability.
2) Upgrade Gateway: a control-plane service that coordinates runs, enforces rollout gates (canary cohorts, quota-based slow-start), and interacts with the Console to display progress and allow manual aborts. The gateway implements a plugin interface for runtime-specific migration steps (db migrations, agent upgrade hooks, custom preflight probes).
3) Preflight hooks and compatibility probes: small, containerized probes that customers can customize (preflight-config). These probes run in-cluster with limited RBAC and report structured results back to the gateway.
4) Rollout gates: implement gating by canary size, success thresholds, latency and error budgets from telemetry, and a time-based backoff with automatic rollback if thresholds are crossed. Gate definitions are pluggable via the Console UI and have defaults tuned for low-risk upgrades.

Acceptance criteria:
- Spec document for THP with state machine diagrams and message formats in Confluence (link below).
- Working prototype of Upgrade Gateway with capability to initiate a run against a sandbox VPC cluster and progress through end-to-end scenario (PREPARE -> COMMIT).
- Preflight probe interface and two example probes (agent health, KV cache integrity).
- Integration tests exercising resumability, idempotence, and forced rollback paths.
- Console integration showing run status and manual abort/rollback controls.
- Runbook and incident playbook for failed upgrades including telemetry dashboard links.

Operational concerns and trade-offs:
- Trade-off: synchronous vs asynchronous validation. Chose asynchronous validation for long-running checks to avoid blocking control-plane threads; this requires careful state reconciliation to avoid flapping.
- Trade-off: central coordinator vs distributed orchestration. We implement a central Upgrade Gateway for orchestration and per-cluster agents to execute steps; this reduces cross-cluster coordination complexity but requires robust reconcilers for gateway-agent communication failures.
- Security: all control messages are signed; all probes run with least-privilege. Security review required before shipping to production.

Backward compatibility and LTS handling:
- The gateway understands LTS channels and supports target-version pinning. Migration recipes can define compatibility validators that map older LTS schemas to new ones. For emergency LTS pinning, customers can create a hold that prevents the gateway from scheduling runs for their cohort.

Telemetry and observability:
- Emit structured events per THP transition (namespaced by customer, cluster, run id).
- Add Prometheus metrics for run counts, durations, success/fail ratios, and per-gate pass rates.
- Dashboard: private-upgrade-runs (Grafana) with heatmaps for rollback frequency and top failure probes.

User flows covered:
- Automated upgrade (scheduled): gateway runs preflight across cohorts, promotes on success; defaults to conservative canary then ramp.
- Manual upgrade: operator triggers run via Console, inspects probes, and confirms commits.
- Dry-run: simulated runs that exercise compatibility checks without mutating state.

Next milestones:
- 2025-03-20: complete THP spec and plugin API (owner: Diego)
- 2025-04-01: deliver Gateway prototype with sandbox run capability (owner: Diego)
- 2025-04-10: complete integration tests and Console linkage (owner: Platform Test)

Notes on rollout safety: include a default 5-minute quiesce window after each state transition to let monitoring catch regressions. The gateway will prefer automatic rollbacks on high-severity regressions but expose manual override for customer SREs.

Risks:
- Incomplete compatibility validators could cause partial data loss in edge migrations; mitigations: safe-mode (snapshot+dry-run) and mandatory snapshot before MIGRATE.
- Air-gapped artifact delivery complexity: require customers to provide verified registries; include validation steps in PREPARE.

Acceptance sign-off: Product (Marta Chen), Security (Kyle Nguyen), and Platform Reliability (Liam O'Connor).
